title: `fire_unit_until` still blocks until the whole minute pass ends
description: `fire_unit_until()` calls `run(["mt-run", *mt_run_args], sudo=True, check=False, stream=True)` at `scripts/cutover_common.py:356`. That launches `deploy/mt-run`, whose `start_and_stream()` starts the unit with `--no-block` and then waits in `while is_running "${unit}"; do sleep 2; done` at `deploy/mt-run:127-129`; `subprocess.run()` therefore does not return until the oneshot finishes. As a result, `wait_for_unit_or_line()` at `scripts/cutover_common.py:318-331` and `stop_unit()` at `scripts/cutover_common.py:337-339` are unreachable while the unbounded backfill is running, defeating the new "stop once the trailing phase line lands" behavior described in `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:174-182`. The interactive `Ctrl-C detaches` trap at `deploy/mt-run:125` does not make Python's `subprocess.run()` keep waiting; it propagates `KeyboardInterrupt`. The new tests at `test/unit/test_cutover_921.py:441-490` patch `cutover_common.run` to return immediately, so they assert the intended control flow but not the real wrapper contract.

title: Firing-time selection uses `.replace()` on a non-UTC database timestamp
description: `MINUTE_PASS_FIRING_TIMES_UTC` and `deploy/systemd/mt-minute-pass.timer:7-8` define `04:05`/`13:05` UTC, but `collecting_firing_finished_at()` calls `close.replace(hour=firing.hour, minute=firing.minute, ...)` on `session.session_close_utc` without first converting it to UTC. The same file acknowledges at `src/manta_trading/cli/commands/minute_session_mass.py:260-265` that psycopg returns `timestamptz` in the connection zone (`America/Denver` in production) and fixes only the display label with `.astimezone(UTC)`. With a Denver-zone close, `04:05` is built as 04:05 MDT/MST (10:05/11:05 UTC), so the +3h verdict becomes 13:05/14:05 UTC instead of 07:05 UTC. The changed boundary tests at `test/unit/cli/commands/test_data_health.py:192-260` use UTC-aware datetimes and do not exercise the production timezone path.

title: Repair/verify command failures can be reported as a complete cutover
description: `_repair()` runs the production Python with `check=False`, prints a non-zero exit message, and returns only `stdout + stderr`. `_verify_when_fresh()` at `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:200-213` and `main()` at `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:264-273` decide acceptance solely from the absence of `"FAIL"` and `"[WAIT]"` in that text. A crashed `--verify` (traceback, DB/connection error, or the `RepairScanTimeout` branch in `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py#main`, which prints `"scan refused"` and returns `EXIT_REFUSED`) contains neither marker, so the script can print `CUTOVER COMPLETE` and return 0. Non-zero `--apply`/`--check` failures are also logged but ignored before the script continues firing passes. Propagate the child return code or use a structured status instead of inferring success from free-form output.

title: The sudoers policy is inconsistent with the cutover commands and is not least-privilege
description: The file claims at `deploy/sudoers.d/manta-ops:1-4` to allow "exactly the commands those scripts issue, nothing wider", but `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:97-99` issues `sudo /opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/python scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py ...` and no alias permits that command. Conversely, `MT_RUN *` at `deploy/sudoers.d/manta-ops:8` permits arbitrary arguments to the root-executed wrapper; `deploy/mt-run:148-166` passes those arguments through to `/opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/mt` after sourcing the production env file. `MT_INSTALL` at `deploy/sudoers.d/manta-ops:9` also grants NOPASSWD root to a script under the operator's home checkout; if that path is writable by `manta`, it is an arbitrary-root grant. Install the privileged installer to a root-owned path, enumerate exact repair commands, and avoid the broad `mt-run *` rule.

title: The new cutover log does not contain the actual cutover report
description: `start_log()`/`say()` tee only `say(...)` lines. The repair script's acceptance output is emitted with `print(output)` at `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:102`; pass streaming output and the polling lines in `scripts/cutover_common.py:318-331` are also plain `print` or inherited stdout. That contradicts the script docstring at `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:21` ("every action is logged") and the `full narration` label at `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:278`: the file misses the PASS/FAIL/WAIT numbers and journal output that motivated the log. `test/unit/test_cutover_921.py:501-508` only proves two `say()` lines are written, not that the report is auditable.

title: Session judgement counts bars that ingestion will discard
description: `bar_timestamp()` at `src/manta_trading/data/acquisition/daemon/minute_sessions.py:27-40` validates only the timestamp, and `sessions_without_bars()` at `:43-61` treats any parsed in-session timestamp as collected. But `src/manta_trading/data/acquisition/daemon/minute.py#_bar_to_row` skips bars with missing, null, non-finite, or non-positive OHLC values before `_insert_minute_bars()` writes anything. `judge_chunk_by_sessions()` is called at `src/manta_trading/data/acquisition/daemon/minute.py:902-909` using the raw response bars; a single in-session bar with a valid timestamp but invalid prices can therefore produce `SUCCESS`, delete/shrink the gap row, and insert zero rows. The new fixtures in `test/unit/data/acquisition/daemon/test_minute_sessions.py:22-36` only build valid price bars. Judge the validated insertable rows (or the insert result), and add a malformed-price regression test.

title: Changed import blocks violate the required Ruff import-order rule
description: `pyproject.toml`'s `[tool.ruff.lint]` block selects `I`, so Ruff enforces import grouping/sorting. The changed `from cutover_common import ...` block at `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:45-58` is not sorted; neither is `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py:59-66` (`cagg_freshness_for_session, CheckReport, RepairScanTimeout, build...`), `src/manta_trading/data/acquisition/daemon/minute.py:16-64` (local application imports interleaved out of order), or `test/unit/test_repair_921.py:27-33`. These will be flagged by the mechanically enforced Ruff baseline. Run `ruff check --fix` and `ruff format` on the touched files.

title: The new cagg freshness probe bypasses the guarded shared helper
description: `cagg_freshness_for_session()` reimplements the refresh-job lookup with a plain `SELECT stats.last_successful_finish`, an inner `JOIN`, no `nullif(..., '-infinity'::timestamptz)`, no `scheduled`/`last_run_status` signals, and no statement timeout. The established helper at `src/manta_trading/market/maintenance/cagg_freshness.py:70-82` already normalizes `-infinity`, uses a `LEFT JOIN`, and `src/manta_trading/market/maintenance/cagg_freshness.py#_set_probe_timeout` bounds every probe with `CAGG_FRESHNESS_PROBE_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT`. `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py#run_verify` calls this partial probe and then `fetch_session_mass()` directly without `assert_cagg_fresh`, so acceptance has a second, weaker freshness implementation. Reuse the shared verdict/augment seam or extract one bounded helper; also add a never-refreshed-policy test.

title: The bounded firing waits for the entire pass before checking its journal
description: `run(["mt-run", ...])` is synchronous. The `mt-run` wrapper starts the unit and then waits for it to stop (`deploy/mt-run:127-129`), so `wait_for_unit_or_line` cannot observe the trailing-complete marker while the pass is running. The cutover therefore cannot stop the minute unit at that marker as intended; it waits for the full, potentially unbounded backfill instead.

title: A failed verification can be reported as a successful cutover
description: `_repair` records a nonzero exit code but still returns the output, and the final acceptance check only looks for `FAIL` and `[WAIT]`. For example, `--verify` can exit nonzero with a scan-refused diagnostic and neither marker; this check then treats the cutover as successful. Check the subprocess return code and require an explicit successful verification result before reporting completion.

title: The sudoers installer rule runs a checkout script as root
description: `MT_INSTALL` permits root execution of `install-production.sh` from the operator checkout. If the operator can modify that checkout, they can alter the script and have the altered code run as root. Do not authorize a root-run script from a user-writable path; use a root-owned, integrity-controlled copy or another mechanism that validates the executable before privilege elevation.

title: The mt-run sudo rule grants more root access than the cutover needs
description: `/usr/local/bin/mt-run *` allows every wrapper mode and argument, not just the pass commands used by the cutover. Other arguments are forwarded to the production CLI, which runs as root when invoked through this rule. Narrow the allowed command arguments to the intended operations.

title: The sudoers fragment does not authorize the repair command
description: The cutover’s `_repair` invokes `/opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/python scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py ...` with `sudo` (`scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:96`), but this fragment grants no permission for that command. With this fragment as the intended restricted grant, the cutover will be denied at its first repair invocation unless another sudoers rule separately authorizes it.

title: The sudoers rule does not authorize the repair/verify command the cutover runs
description:
The file's own header claims it contains "Exactly the commands those scripts issue, nothing wider". `_repair()` (`scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:93-100`) runs `sudo /opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/python scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py <mode>` — with `sudo=True` — and that command appears in none of `MT_UNITS`, `MT_RUN`, `MT_INSTALL`, `MT_READ`, or `MT_GIT`. On a host where this file is the operator account's only grant, the cutover's very first repair step (`_repair("--check")`) is refused, because sudoers is allow-list: an unlisted command is denied rather than password-prompted. `sudo -v`, `sudo -u manta-trading git -C /opt/manta-trading rev-parse HEAD` (line 14, matching `cutover_common.install`), `sudo cat /etc/manta-trading.env` (`cutover_common.migrate`), and `sudo systemctl stop/start mt-*` are all covered, so the omission of the repair invocation looks unintentional rather than a deliberate narrowing.

Two related couplings worth pinning while you are here: `MT_INSTALL` hard-codes `/home/manta/source/repos/manta/trading-data/deploy/install-production.sh`, and `cutover_common.install()` now resolves that path as `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "deploy/install-production.sh"` (`scripts/cutover_common.py:132-135`) — nothing checks that the two agree, so a checkout at any other path breaks the install step silently; and this artifact has no drift guard, although the repo already guards its sibling deploy artifacts (`test/unit/deploy/test_units.py` parses the units, the installer's `UNITS` array and `mt-run`). A guard in that module asserting every `sudo`-prefixed command the cutover scripts issue is named by a `Cmnd_Alias` in this file would have caught this omission mechanically.

title: The new cagg-freshness probe drops the `-infinity` normalization slice 168 documents as required
description:
`cagg_freshness_for_session` selects `stats.last_successful_finish` raw. `src/manta_trading/market/maintenance/cagg_freshness.py:68-79` states in the same repository: "`last_successful_finish` is `-infinity` for a policy that has been created but has never completed a run. psycopg cannot load that into a datetime — it raises `DataError` mid-fetch", and normalizes it with `nullif(s.last_successful_finish, '-infinity'::timestamptz)`. The new query has no such guard, so for any cagg whose refresh policy has not yet completed a run (a fresh or rebuilt database — 051 recreates both coverage caggs' policies, and the test tier runs against freshly migrated databases) the fetch raises. `run_verify` (`scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py:255-295`) and `main` catch only `RepairScanTimeout`, so the operator gets a psycopg traceback instead of the `[WAIT]`/`[FAIL]` verdict, and `cutover_921`'s `_verify_when_fresh` never sees the text it branches on.

The same probe also re-spells `'policy_refresh_continuous_aggregate'` as a bare literal in the SQL, while `cagg_freshness.py:58` defines that value as a named constant precisely because it is "the same value `cagg_repair.py` filters on" — the project rule is one definition per value.

title: A chunk with bars but no judgeable session keeps `PARTIAL`, contradicting the stated removal of the weekend tolerance
description:
`judge_chunk_by_sessions` returns the classifier's verdict unchanged when `judged` is empty. `src/manta_trading/data/acquisition/daemon/minute.py:889-901` justifies deleting the old four-day tolerance with "a weekend or holiday tail has no session to be missing, so a chunk whose sessions are all covered is SUCCESS however far its last bar sits before chunk_end" — but a chunk containing *no* session at all is the case where "all its sessions are covered" is vacuously true, and there the code does not return `SUCCESS`.

Concretely: for a range lying wholly between two sessions (the shape a legacy midnight-anchored row takes, e.g. `[Sat 00:00, Sun 00:00]`), `fetch_session_bounds` returns `{}`, so `judged` is empty and a response carrying only the spillover bar keeps the classifier's `PARTIAL`. The removed tolerance (`(chunk_end.date() - latest.date()).days <= 4`) turned exactly that response into `SUCCESS`, which deleted the row. Now the row survives, is re-picked each cycle (it is the most recent actionable gap), and `_advance_minute_gap` increments `attempt_count` each time until it promotes to `RETRY_EXHAUSTED` at `MAX_RETRY_COUNT` — a terminal row that makes `data_status.health` read `FAILED` for that symbol forever, which is the "a unit that is always failed is not an alarm" pathology slice 921 exists to remove.

The behaviour is deliberate and pinned by `test_no_judgeable_session_keeps_the_classifier_verdict` and `test_empty_bounds_judge_nothing`, and the reachable population may now be small because the repair resets in-window rows to session-close ends. I could not verify how many legacy midnight-anchored actionable rows remain in production (`find_truncated_days` and `build_truncated_day_index` ignore them; `count_row_shapes`' `midnight_ended_rows` counter is the only measurement, and terminal legacy rows are excluded from `pick_most_recent_actionable_gap`). Please either confirm the class is empty in production, or state the residual — currently the code comment asserts a property the code does not have for this input.

title: The narration log does not contain the acceptance output it exists to preserve
description: `start_log`/`say` (`scripts/cutover_common.py:41-62`) tee only `say()` lines. The cutover's `_repair()` prints the `--check`/`--apply`/`--verify` bodies with a plain `print(output)`, never `say`, so the numbers the whole slice is judged on are absent from `project-documents/user/notes/921-cutover-<ts>.log`. The same is true of `install()`, `hold_timer()`, `release_timer()` and the "`unit` is running — waiting" polls in `cutover_common`, which all use `print`. The script's closing line tells the operator `full narration: {log_path}`, and the incomplete-run line tells them to "read the FAIL lines" — those FAIL lines are in the terminal and not in the file. The added test (`test_say_tees_to_the_log_file`) asserts only the `say` path, so this gap is invisible to the suite. Given the docstring's premise ("The first 921 cutover's only record was terminal scrollback across two ten-hour firings"), routing the repair/verify output through the log is the point.

title: The minute-pass timer still describes a 30-minute stagger that no longer exists
description: The `Description` (line 2) and the `[Timer]` comment (lines 6-7) say the pass is "staggered 30 minutes behind the daily pass" so the two "never start simultaneously". With the first firing moved to `04:05` and `mt-daily-pass.timer` at `00:35/12:35`, the first firing is 3 h 30 min behind, not 30 minutes; only the `13:05` firing is 30 minutes behind `12:35`. The diff updated the equivalent comment in `deploy/systemd/mt-kalshi-pass.timer` ("00:35/12:35, 04:05/13:05") but left this one stating a schedule the file no longer has — in the file whose firing time the health check's judged-session boundary is derived from.
